I am a PhD student in Buddhist studies at the [International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies](https://www.icabs.ac.jp/), Tokyo, Japan. 

My doctoral thesis is about the translation practice of Kumārajīva (c. 350s–c. 411) and his disciples, focussing in particular on their 406 CE translation of the <em>Vimalakīrtinirdeśa</em>.

My research interests include:<br>
- Buddhist translations and commentaries in East Asia<br>
- The acculturation of Buddhism in Six Dynasties/Early Medieval China<br>
- The permeable relationship between translation and exegesis across Buddhist traditions<br>
- The history of translation and cross-cultural exchange, especially in  premodern Asia<br>
- Historical linguistics, textual criticism and manuscript studies in general, including  computational approaches to philology<br>
